A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Variational Search Distributions by the same authors. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original biological-sequence experiments, including fitness-landscape comparisons, AAV/GFP optimization and supplementary GP-surrogate results in Figures 2, 3 and 5.

after.justification: V3 reports original biological-sequence experiments, MNIST generation, Ehrlich-function optimization, diversity measurements and prior/architecture ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The reverse-KL ELBO, classifier loss and score-function update remain. Algorithm 1 adds a final threshold/model refit and returns generator/classifier parameters instead of collected positive designs. LSTM and transformer instances replace the earlier simple autoregressive instance within the existing modular framework (v1 Appendix B.1; v3 Appendix B.3).

E1.justification: V3 retains all five biological datasets and adds conditional MNIST generation targeting digits 3 and 5, introducing image-generation coverage. It also adds closed-form Ehrlich sequence-optimization benchmarks using POLI and HOLO implementations, extending evaluation beyond the retained experimental landscapes and learned protein oracles.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated genetic-algorithm and LaMBO-2 baselines on the Ehrlich benchmarks (Figures 5 and 8), substantially extending comparison to guided diffusion. It also adds AdaLead curves to the GP-based landscape comparison (v1 Figure 5; v3 Figure 7). LaMBO itself is discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Normalized fitness performance in v1 Equation 18 becomes cumulative unique-sequence fitness in v3 Equation 16, and batch diversity becomes an additional metric. Reported CPE architectures and variational-model configurations change. New protocols include single-round MNIST adaptation and 32-round Ehrlich optimization from 128 initial observations; the retained biological experiments use ten rounds.

E4.justification: The existing GP-surrogate analysis continues in v3 Appendix C.1. New Appendices C.3–C.4 examine batch diversity and systematically compare uniform versus informed priors and independent, transition, LSTM and transformer posterior families. Figure 12 supplies direct ablation evidence beyond v1's qualitative observations about these choices.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly reports five random seeds in Section 4 and Appendix B.2; v1 does not state a run count. Both versions display error bars without clearly identifying their statistic. This establishes additional reporting, not an increase in the number of runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds MNIST samples and classifier results, including approximately 99% balanced accuracy, Ehrlich regret curves, diversity scores and prior/architecture ablation results. Existing biological-landscape and AAV/GFP curves are also revised. Changed architectures and the redefined performance metric prevent interpreting these revisions as controlled, same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1's two optimization-bound propositions survive in v3 Appendix F. New Section 2.4 and Appendices D–E introduce assumptions and proofs for GP variance convergence, conditional-distribution convergence, an expected-hit bound and NTK-based neural-classifier rates. Section 2.2 also corrects the Gaussian probability-of-improvement expression.

C1.justification: V3 adds asymptotic convergence-rate guarantees to its headline contributions and emphasizes learning expressive conditional generative models. The task is explicitly framed as active generation, with generative modeling promoted from a desideratum to requirement R5. V1 claimed effective variational search and empirical competitiveness but did not claim these convergence rates.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations linking expressive-generator gains to generalization and sampling from the adapting distribution. It cautions that diversity alone need not improve search, discusses prior overfitting, and notes that theoretical hit counts include duplicates. Earlier warnings about oracle extrapolation and dependence on informative priors largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses optimization-iteration budgets and AdaLead's kappa setting, adds detailed LSTM/transformer configurations in Table 4, and describes early stopping, augmentation and Ehrlich CNN ensembles. Benchmark-specific settings and revised CPE specifications substantially expand reproducibility information. Previously unstated iteration budgets do not establish a change in actual training duration.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to latent-space optimization, LaMBO/LaMBO-2, guided generation and active level-set estimation, explicitly distinguishing these approaches from VSD. New GP/NTK references support the theoretical analysis, and v3 newly positions DHFR and TrpB as previously unused in machine-learning research.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the introduction, problem formulation, related-work narrative and conclusion around active generation. Dataset descriptions and settings move into expanded Appendix B, supplementary experiments become Appendix C, and the former Section 2.4 moves to Appendix F. New theory occupies Section 2.4 and Appendices D–E.

P2.justification: V3 adds digit-sample galleries, Ehrlich plots, diversity panels, ablation displays and an architecture-configuration table. The three-panel BBO display becomes a two-by-three dataset/model grid. Tables 1 and 2 change their rows or columns, and existing result figures receive revised legends and performance-axis scales.

improvement.justification: V1's high-dimensional validation relied on learned oracles, while its theoretical discussion offered only elementary optimization bounds. V3 adds closed-form Ehrlich comparisons, conditional convergence analyses and direct prior/diversity diagnostics, substantially strengthening evidence about applicability and design choices. Expanded settings improve reproducibility. Restrictive theoretical assumptions, undefined error-bar statistics and changed evaluation settings still limit interpretation, but the gains in evidence and transparency are substantial.
